reasoning: Classify elements of {1,...,100} by residue mod 7. Since 100 = 14*7 + 2, residues 1 and 2 occur 15 times each; residues 0,3,4,5,6 occur 14 times each. Two elements sum to a multiple of 7 iff their residues are complementary: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), or both 0. So the subset can contain elements from at most one class of each complementary pair, and at most one element ≡ 0. Upper bound: 15 (class 1) + 15 (class 2) + 14 (class 3 or 4) + 1 = 45. Construction achieving 45: {n : n ≡ 1, 2, or 3 (mod 7), 1 ≤ n ≤ 100} ∪ {7}, i.e. {1,8,...,99} ∪ {2,9,...,100} ∪ {3,10,...,94} ∪ {7}. Any two distinct elements have residue sum in {2,3,4,5,6,1,2,3} mod 7, never 0.
